_doc: Point-in-time retrospective. Every input was public on as_of; see sources. Hindsight lives only in outcome.json.
methodology: house v2 (EPP-distance adjustment), 6-section format; retro method r2: scenario inputs derived from dated facts by frozen rules (retro/README.md); ratings, education and information signals

pit_profile.why: The McGraw-Hill Companies 'is a leading global information services provider serving the financial services, education and business information markets' (Item 1); Item 1A: 'The Company’s results could be adversely affected by a reduction in the volume of debt securities issued in domestic and/or global capital markets', and under 'Cyclical Nature of Customers’ Businesses' 'The School Education Group and the industry it serves are influenced strongly by the magnitude and timing of state adoption opportunities' (the customers' adoption cycle, not the company's own earnings called cyclical); a fall in debt issuance, state adoptions or advertising cuts revenue, and no disruption theme is live for the business on this date

classification.quality_note: The McGraw-Hill Companies 'is a leading global information services provider serving the financial services, education and business information markets' (Item 1); Item 1A: 'The Company’s results could be adversely affected by a reduction in the volume of debt securities issued in domestic and/or global capital markets', and under 'Cyclical Nature of Customers’ Businesses' 'The School Education Group and the industry it serves are influenced strongly by the magnitude and timing of state adoption opportunities' (the customers' adoption cycle, not the company's own earnings called cyclical); a fall in debt issuance, state adoptions or advertising cuts revenue, and no disruption theme is live for the business on this date. durable franchise (obsolescence risk 2/5); price cheap; Ratio B 0.40x; -19% to EPP floor; model-vs-market gap +1.06; conservative 2yr +62%.

BEAR.desc: EPS -19.3%/yr (worst year FY99-FY09, capped at 0%); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS +5.7%/yr (Q4 revenue + margin + buyback); P/E at its 10-yr median

BULL.desc: EPS +8.2%/yr (FY99-FY09 CAGR); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +36.5%/yr (best 2-yr run FY99-FY09); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: MHP (retrospective, 2010-01-27) ◉ BUY — Ratio B 0.40x (38.4% downside to Bear $22 / +96.0% upside to Bull $70) | Adj composite 2.71 vs market 1.65: gap +1.06 [UNDERVALUED] | -19% above the EPP floor $44 (17x FY10E $2.60) | Conservative 2-yr case: +61.8% total (+30.9%/yr) | At 13.7x FY10E the 15% hurdle price $47 sits at or below the BASE case; Financial Services revenue +10.6% in Q4 2009, forward revenues +3.3% (no FY10 revenue guide in numbers, Q4 2009 growth); no disruption theme has dated evidence.
